rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING MALASAKIT CENTERS IN ALL ACCREDITED PUBLIC HOSPITALS ALL OVER THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Aims to provide indigent patients with zero balance billing by institutionalizing the Malasakit Center in efforts to unburden them of documentary requirements for them to avail of various medical assistance and treatments in hospitals.

Proposes a one-stop service center of government services comprised of different agencies which can provide help to families of patients who wish to settle medical expenses through expediting of complicated processes in availing of services primarily for, but not limited to, financial assistance. Intends to bring government services closer to the poor and marginalized people as agencies will be house in one location.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05477

rows.mother_status: Pending With Rules (Included in OB on 2020-01-28)
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLES 96 AND 124 OF THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to eliminate all forms of discrimination against women in both the public and private spheres, to
promote equality between women and men and to advance women's rights.

Proposes to remove the portion in Articles 96 and 124 of the Family Code which gives preference to the
husband's decision over that of the wife in case of disagreement on the administration and enjoyment
of the conjugal or community property.

Intends to preserve and safeguard conjugal or community properties from unilateral and reckless decisions that are often resorted to when conflict occurs between the husband and the wife.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06078

rows.abstract:
Proposes to amend Art.55 (1), (5) and (6) under the grounds for legal separation, whereas Art.55(1) is to
consider not only the number of times violence is perpetrated but also the severity or gravity of the physical or sexual violence committed; while Art. 55 (5) and (6) are additional grounds such as excessive gambling and bisexuality of the respondents.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING TITLE VI OF E.O. 209 AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE BY REMOVING AND/OR ERASING CLASSIFICATION BETWEEN LEGITIMATE, ILLEGITIMATE AND LEGITIMATED (FILIATION OF) CHILDREN, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Intends to ensure that the best interests of the child must be the primary consideration in all actions 
concerning children, and that children shall be protected against all forms of discrimination.

Offers remedy to the existing provisions of Family Code where it discriminates against children conceived or born out of wedlock of parents who, at the time of the conception of the former were disqualified by an impediment to marry each other which is prejudicial against such \"illegitimate\" children who cannot and should not be faulted for their parent's marital impediment/s.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2019-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLES 14, 211 AND 225 OF THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to amend several provisions in the Family code to remove the preferential treatment for the
father's decision in matter's concerning children, from exercising authority over their persons
and properties to withholding or giving consent to their child's marriage.

Intends to harmonize the Family Code with the Magna Carta of Women and shall serve as responses to 
our international commitments sustained on the Elimination of all Forms of Discrimination Against Women and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child.

rows.abstract:
Seeks to establish and maintain a cancer center that shall specialize in cancer treatment, enhance the noble undertaking of cancer research, provide state-of-the art training of medical and technical personnel, develop programs for the prevention and early detection of cancer and attract the best cancer specialists in the country to render service for indigent patients at affordable rates.

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2020-09-22, transmitted to the Senate on 2020-09-24 and received by the Senate on 2020-09-24
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF DISASTER RESILIENCE, DEFINING ITS POWER AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Proposes to create a truly empowered department that will focus on natural hazards and disasters, characterized by unity of command, a science-and ICT-based approach, and the capacity to take charge of three (3) key result areas: 1) disaster risk reduction; 2) disaster preparedness and response; and 3) recovery, rehabilitation, etc.

Provides for key elements and features of the proposed Department as follows: a) unity of command, abolishing the Climate Change Commission and the NDRRMC; b) full-time focus on resilience to natural hazards; c) temporary take-over or direct any private utility for urgent public purpose; d) rationalized judicious and expeditious use of funds to help ensure the timely support where urgently and critically needed; e) innovative and responsive procurement mechanisms; f) Science and ICT-based approach to ensure real time access to relevant information; g) highly specialized functions and highly-skilled personnel requirements; h) institutional partnerships with LGUs, NGOs, and academia.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05989

rows.author: G097
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE INSTITUTIONALIZATION, DEVELOPMENT, TRAINING, ORGANIZATION AND ADMINISTRATION OF BASIC RESERVE OFFICERS TRAINING CORPS (ROTC) IN GRADES 11 AND 12 IN PUBLIC AND PRIVATE EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7077, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'CITIZEN ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES RESERVIST ACT', AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Seeks to establish a mandatory two (2)-year Basic ROTC program for students in Grades 11 and 12 in public and private education institutions with the objective of producing well-trained and prepared reservists for military and civil service and instill patriotism, moral and spiritual virtues and respect for human rights and adherence to the Constitution.

States that student who fails to undergo the mandatory Basic ROTC shall not be qualified for graduation with the following exemptions: a.) those who are physically or psychologically unfit, as certified by the AFP Surgeon General or his authorized officer; b.) those who have undergone or are undergoing similar military training; c.) those who were chosen to serve as the school´s varsity players; and d.) those who may be exempted from training for valid reasons as approved by the DND.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2019-08-27
